findings.summary: gate_yield.py cmd_rollup registered the per_gate key BEFORE inspecting the event name, so ANY non-gate producer riding the one write path minted a phantom zero-yield gate row in the retirement instrument — the integration-adversary PROVED IT BY EXECUTION at plan re-review (three usage events -> `| readable-surface | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |`, then `candidates` reported the non-gate in its measured denominator) and both adversaries independently converged on the same seam. Fixed at the owner: the ROSTER decision (closed GATE_EVENTS vocabulary) is now separate from the COUNTING decision, for every future producer; usage events route to their own table; unknown events stay ignored-without-a-row.

The approved plan's first D5 design classified host from the bin's __file__ path / an installer marker and suppressed logging when unrecognised. This repo has no .claude/bin/ and no marker — it dogfoods via the marketplace plugin — so BOTH real invocation paths classified as not-Claude and the experiment would have produced a permanently empty usage record, auto-reading as `kill` on 2026-09-30 regardless of use. Replaced at the producer: _common.log_yield_event stamps host from host-runtime-provided signals (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR / TDD_PLAYBOOK_PROJECT_ROOT), unknown is LABELLED and still logged, never suppressed — all three directions pinned explicitly (an inherited session env would pass at home and fail in CI).

test_agents.py's opus-pin check iterated a hand list with no completeness guard, so the four new judgment agents would have shipped with `model: opus` NEVER CHECKED, green. Guard added BEFORE the agents: PINNED|INHERIT must equal the real directory, vacuity-guarded, with a planted unclassified-agent detector.

The first full gate run went RED at the calibration stage: five new gate surfaces (4 briefs + /readable) had no covering ledger entries — the gate-surface ledger working as designed. Entries registered with expect=up for the four briefs (each born with its plant/control pair, so the first live run scores recall and FP from zero) and expect=none for the narration command. An auto-checkpoint landed the surfaces before the ledger commit; per the recovered 2026-08-07 precedent this is in-window late registration against the true baseline (3fafc9e), stated in the commit message rather than smoothed over.
findings.disposition: Ledger entries L-20260812-01..05 committed separately (e15bd84); ledger check exits 0 vs v1.33.1; the same-commit blind spot remains dated debt on gate-surface-ledger.

findings.summary: Twice during release verification the operator (the model) piped a checker into grep/head and echoed $? — reading the FILTER's exit code as the checker's, exactly the §4a discarded-truth sin this repo's gate script warns about. Both self-caught on re-run (the scoreboard planted probe first reported a false rc, and the as-of expiry proof reported rc=0 from head); both re-verified unpiped before any claim was recorded. Named here because a verification habit that survives two occurrences in one release is a candidate for the next planted-error probe.
findings.disposition: All recorded claims re-verified with unpiped rc. The exitcode_guard exists for exactly this and ships opt-in; whether to opt it in for this repo is David's call, noted not smuggled.

findings.summary: PAID ON EVIDENCE 2026-08-13. Live calibration ran for all four pairs. security 3/3+3/3 PASS, test-quality 3/3+3/3 PASS at the haiku lower bound. adoption 3/3+3/3 PASS after its CONTROL was found mis-authored (below), with the plant oracle TIGHTENED to require naming the defect. observability 3/3+3/3 PASS at OPUS, its production tier, while its control is FLAKY at haiku (2/3 AMBER twice; a 3-rep reproduction went 3/3). The AMBER rows STAY in the record — never retried into green (section 7) — and the remaining obligation is re-scoped as dated debt observability-haiku-flakiness (2026-09-30) rather than closed by re-rolling.
findings.disposition: PAID ON EVIDENCE 2026-08-13 (docs/calibration/history.md), not closed by a repo test — no suite can prove a live model run happened, so this is incorporated rather than verified_closed. Residual obligation re-scoped as dated debt observability-haiku-flakiness (2026-09-30).

findings.summary: The new test_readable_surface.py DELETED TDD_PLAYBOOK_YIELD_LOG rather than redirecting it, so readable_surface.py fell through to the repo's real .claude/playbook-yield.jsonl; the next live calibration ran gate_yield rollup and drained 24 fabricated uses into the committed docs/calibration/usage.md — the exact record the 2026-09-30 keep/kill decision reads. The pollution pin I wrote for this release lives in calibration/test_harness.py, which snapshots the file when the HARNESS starts, by which time this suite had already written: a pin in the wrong suite. Fixed by redirecting unconditionally (the test_gate_yield.py precedent) and pinning BOTH the committed record and the raw log inside the offending suite; proven red-first by reverting the isolation, which makes the new pin fail. Fabricated rows purged before any commit.

The adoption control sat at 0/3 through an agent fix. Capturing the agent's actual output BEFORE touching it again showed the agent was RIGHT: it built the required table, computed the verdict mechanically, and named FOUR genuine S40 dead ends left standing in the fixture (missing-arg IndexError, non-numeric ValueError, out-of-range ValueError, bare print('denied')). The control had cleaned only the unknown-command path, so it was never clean code and could not measure restraint. A fourth 'fix' would have trained a working verifier to ignore real defects and turned the calibration green on a WORSE agent. This is a third category beyond 'fix the agent, never the plant' — a MIS-AUTHORED CONTROL — and the discipline separating it from rationalisation is EVIDENCE BEFORE THE EDIT. Pair re-authored to differ only in the planted defect; plant oracle tightened; both directions then 3/3.
findings.disposition: Pair re-authored to differ only in the planted defect; plant oracle TIGHTENED to require naming it; both directions then 3/3 live (history.md). SEVERITY IS P2 BY THIS REPO'S OWN CONVENTION, not convenience: P1 here means closed by a mechanical test (v1.33.0's AGENTS.md finding), P2 means resolved with a recorded disposition where the resolution is not a test (v1.33.0's tag_guard finding). This one's proof is a live model run, which no repo suite can assert. A structural pair-invariant test WAS added (test_plant_control_pairs_differ_only_in_the_planted_defect) and is explicitly NOT cited as closure: planting the original defect shape showed it PASSES cleanly — the broken pair had exactly one differing edit at the same anchor and was semantically wrong via the untouched fixture. Citing it would be gate-by-proxy. The transferable rule — EVIDENCE BEFORE THE EDIT when a control fails — lives in ledger L-20260813-02 and this record.

findings.summary: Two of four new agents failed live in the SAME way: each brief hunts a broad list while each plant/control pair tests ONE question, so where the fixture is legitimately thin on the other items (no README, no status surface, no telemetry) a weak doer imports out-of-scope gaps into the verdict and flags clean work. Fixed in observability and adoption by a SCOPE RULE (a named focus question bounds the verdict; everything else is a note) plus a computed verdict table. security and test-quality passed 2/2 but partly BECAUSE this fixture is clean on their other hunt rows — the same latent mismatch exists there, untouched, because editing green agents without a failing test to prove the edit right is the move this repo forbids.
